task: Implement user-level model override enforcement for project admins to configure and enforce model access overrides for individual or bulk-selected users, with precedence over project settings, fallback logic, and platform disablement hard stops.

component_scope.label: XL
component_scope.reason: 5 components across 2–3 layers: new API endpoints (admin CRUD), UserModelOverrideService, UserModelOverride repository, ModelAvailabilityService extension with new precedence logic, and invocation resolver integration point. New abstractions (UserModelOverrideService, 4-tier precedence chain) span Service and Repository layers.

requirements_clarity.label: M
requirements_clarity.reason: Core requirements clear: admin-scoped override, 4-tier precedence (platform disable → user override → project whitelist → default), bulk operations, validation against project constraints. Minor implementation unknowns: platform disablement integration point (config file vs. database table), bulk operation atomicity semantics, API endpoint naming and structure. These are 1–2 light questions, not fundamental gaps.

technical_risk.label: XXL
technical_risk.reason: Security-sensitive precedence chain (user override must not grant access to project-disallowed models); validation required at two points: set-time (prevent creation of invalid override) and invocation-time (catch project whitelist changes after override creation). No existing codebase pattern for 4-tier fallback chain; current ModelAvailabilityService implements only 2–3 tiers. No existing parameterized test template for edge cases of multi-level precedence. Invocation-time model lookup adds database query per LLM call; performance implications if not cached. Rollback via feature flag mitigates but does not eliminate deployment risk.

file_change_estimate.label: XL
file_change_estimate.reason: Estimated 8–10 modified files: ModelAvailabilityService (precedence chain integration), Application model (possibly platform_disabled_models), Router/API security helpers, User Management Service (validation), RouterChatModel (invocation integration point), Config module (feature flags), ModelAvailabilityService test suite (4-tier edge cases), API response models (new UserModelOverride schema). Estimated 4–6 new files: UserModelOverride SQLModel table definition, UserModelOverrideService, UserModelOverride repository, API router (or router extension), Alembic migration, test_user_model_override_service.py, test_user_model_override_endpoints.py. Total 12–16 files across 4+ directories (service/llm, core, rest_api/routers, data/repositories, external/alembic/versions, tests).

dependencies.label: S
dependencies.reason: No new third-party packages required. SQLModel, SQLAlchemy, FastAPI already in use. Database access patterns established. Configuration only: new environment variables (PLATFORM_MODEL_OVERRIDE_ENABLED, PLATFORM_DISABLED_MODELS) are simple strings/booleans, no version changes. Alembic already in project; no version updates.

affected_layers.label: L
affected_layers.reason: 4 distinct layers: API (new endpoints for override CRUD, admin gating), Service (UserModelOverrideService, ModelAvailabilityService extension), DB-Persistence (new UserModelOverride table with foreign keys to users and applications, Alembic migration), Invocation/Core (RouterChatModel or model resolver integration). Schema migration required. Not cross-system (internal feature only).

key_reasoning.reason: 5 components across 2–3 layers with 2 new abstractions (UserModelOverrideService, 4-tier precedence chain) maps to XL: new service orchestration layer required to coordinate user override, project whitelist, and platform disablement.

XXL: Security-sensitive precedence chain with validation required at two distinct points (set-time and invocation-time). No existing codebase pattern for 4-tier fallback; current ModelAvailabilityService covers 2–3 tiers. No parameterized test template for multi-level precedence edge cases (security red flag: validation gap across two points). Performance implications per-invocation (database lookup) if not cached. Pattern exists (ModelAvailabilityService) but security validation gap is a divergence.

XL: Estimated 12–16 total files (8–10 modified + 4–6 new) across 4+ directories. Modified: existing service, models, routers, tests. New: service implementation, repository, API router, migration, dedicated test files. Scope matches XL threshold (11–15 files).
L: 4 distinct layers (API, Service, DB-Persistence, Invocation/Core) with schema migration (new table + foreign keys). Not cross-system; internal integration only.

red_flags_applied: Security red flag (access control): User override must not grant access to project-disallowed models. Validation required at set-time (prevent creation) and invocation-time (catch project whitelist changes). Existing ModelAvailabilityService pattern does not cover user-scope override security; validation gap is a divergence. Technical Risk bumped from L (4) to XXL (6).

Technical red flag (defensive pattern): No existing test template covers 4-tier precedence chain (platform disable → user override → project whitelist → default) with all combinations. Acceptance criteria enumerate this specific edge case coverage, and current test suite covers only 2–3 tiers. Technical Risk bumped again from XL (5) to XXL (6).
